argument_macro_structure.dominant_argument_form: Refutation by framework shift (metaphysical paradigm replacement) combined with conditional proof and reductio ad absurdum against the opponent's implicit assumptions.
argument_macro_structure.premise_explicitness: Moderate - key premises (A-theory, B-theory, divine atemporality) are explicitly stated, but some logical transitions (e.g., grounding of truth values) are asserted rather than fully formalized.

argumentative_quality.dialectical_reasonableness: High - the text fairly reconstructs Ostler's argument before attacking it, and systematically addresses counterarguments (memory, causal loops).
argumentative_quality.logical_relevance: High - all premises and objections directly target the core incompatibility thesis.
argumentative_quality.premise_acceptability: Moderate - the argument's success hinges entirely on the acceptance of B-theory (eternalism) and a specific model of divine atemporality, which are highly contested metaphysical positions.

distinctions_drawn: Human temporal intuition vs. divine perspective
Retroactive causation vs. holistic determination of truth values
explicit_definitions_given: A-theory: time flows, past is fixed, future is open, present is privileged.
B-theory: time is a static block, all times are equally real, relations are 'earlier than'/'later than'.
Divine atemporality: God apprehends all moments simultaneously in a single eternal present.

dialectical_engagement.objection_handling: The text anticipates and refutes two major objections: (1) the 'problem of memory' (how can God know a changing future?) and (2) the 'causal loop' paradox (how can an action at t2 retroactively determine a belief at t1?). Both are dismissed as pseudo-problems generated by A-theoretic intuitions.
objections_raised: If God's knowledge is like memory, then a change in the future would falsify God's past belief.
If an agent's choice at t2 grounds God's belief at t1, this creates a causal loop (effect precedes cause).

epistemic_stance_and_voice.certainty_language_frequency: Low - the text uses conditional and hypothetical language ('If reality is fundamentally B-theoretic...', 'If we separate our human intuitions...'), indicating a conditional defense rather than an unconditional proof.

method_and_evidence.evidence_type: Primarily a priori conceptual analysis and metaphysical reasoning. No empirical evidence is cited. The authority of Boethius and Aquinas is invoked to support the historical pedigree of divine atemporality.
named_thought_experiments: The Causal Loop scenario (agent at t2 altering God's belief at t1)
The Memory Problem (God's knowledge modeled on human memory)

philosophical_orientation.grounding: Metaphysical (ontology of time and divine nature).
philosophical_orientation.sentiment: Neutral/analytical - no emotional rhetoric; purely logical and metaphysical exposition.
philosophical_orientation.thematic_focus: Philosophy of religion (divine foreknowledge), metaphysics of time (eternalism vs. presentism), free will (libertarianism).

structural_organization.structure_type: Problem-solution / Thesis-antithesis-synthesis. The text presents Ostler's incompatibilist thesis (antithesis), identifies its hidden A-theoretic assumption, introduces the B-theoretic framework (synthesis), and systematically re-evaluates each component of the original argument (fixity, memory, causation) under the new framework.

summary_of_core_decisions: The text's core strategic decision is to shift the debate from the nature of divine knowledge to the nature of time itself. It argues that Ostler's incompatibilism is not a logical truth but a metaphysical artifact of A-theory. By adopting B-theory (eternalism) and an atemporal God, the 'fixed past' becomes a mere coordinate in a block universe, and the 'power to do otherwise' is redefined as the holistic determination of truth values across the block, thereby dissolving the paradox without sacrificing libertarian freedom or divine omniscience.

thesis_commitment.conclusion_type: Conditional (If B-theory is true, then compatibility follows).
thesis_commitment.hedging_density_in_final_paragraph: Moderate - the final paragraphs use conditional phrasing ('If reality is fundamentally B-theoretic...', 'If we separate our human intuitions...'), indicating the argument's validity is contingent on the acceptance of its metaphysical premises.
